verdict: routes.js clears all fifteen numbered acceptance criteria under execution, not inspection: node --check passes, the export list matches the pinned contract exactly, a 4,500-case sweep found no input for which quote()/meridianQuote() throws or returns a non-object, and no case where Meridian is cheaper or faster than an at-ceiling unescorted player quote (the dominance guard fires and is real, not a comment). hops() returns -1, inReach(null) returns false, PHASE=1 carries the promotion criteria as prose with no Phase 2 penalty reachable in code, and greps find no window/Profile/Corp/Forge/await/fetch/random/.from(/.rpc(/discord/webhook/upload. The commentary is denser than the bar file and most of it is verifiably true: FR_CONVOY_RISK 30 / FR_CONVOY_ESC_CUT 22 / FR_CONVOY_RISK_MIN 4 and the 120000ms floor are exact at index.html:61128-61140; the rigs.data.js negative-points vs GARAGE_RIG_FX fraction unit trap is real and subtle; the depot 'radius: 3 + lv' is exactly production.data.js:387; index.js really does re-export under routes:{...} (index.js:814) and really does store a refusal object as a truthy quote (index.js:653), which the file documents as drift rather than leaving to be found. What it does not do is reconcile with the authority it names. sql/038 was on disk eleven minutes before routes.js and this file calls its transport_quote() THE AUTHORITY, then disagrees with it on risk, ETA, same-node routes and the NPC fare without a word.
biggest_gap: routes.js declares sql/038's transport_quote() the authority and warns that disagreement is 'the worst bug class this repo has', then silently diverges from it on four numbers and one whole route class, with no reconciliation note: (1) RISK - client is base 30 + 4/hop, escort -22 points, clamp [4,95]; server is least(max_risk_pct 45, ceil(hops * risk_pct_per_hop 4)) with escort as a x0.4 multiplier and no base. A 1-hop haul prints 30% to the player and books a 4% contract. (2) ETA - client hopMs 120000 (2 min/hop) divided by rig speed; server v_eta := v_hops * minutes_per_hop (25) and ignores rig speed entirely. A 5-hop haul shows '10m' and runs 125 minutes. (3) SAME-NODE - client returns an ok, priced quote for fromId===toId ('a same-node haul still bills one hop', price 500 in test); transport_quote() returns error 'same_node' outright, so the client prices a route the server will never dispatch. (4) MERIDIAN FARE - client is ceil(ceil(median*2.5)*units*hops)+1 (the +1 dominance edge always fires because refPrice === price); server is ceil(median*2.5*units*hops). At median 41, 100 units, 5 hops that is 51,501 shown vs 51,250 charged, which also falsifies the file's own claim that rounding up 'can only ever over-quote by <1 Cinder'. (5) ESCORT SURCHARGE - client sheet 25% flat; server uses the carrier's own tariff->>'escort_pct'. Fix: add a DRIFT block naming sql/038 line-for-line, move hopMs/riskPerHop/base risk/escort cut into the sheet with the server's defaults (25 min/hop, 4/hop, no base, x0.4, max 45), refuse or flag same-node, and either drop the +1 edge or state that it is a deliberate over-quote.
evidence: node --check public/src/transport/routes.js -> OK. Fuzz (13 hostile inputs x 2 entry points): 'totality fails: 0'. Sweep of 4,500 (median, units, rigSpeed, rigCargo, escort, route) combinations: 'dominance price fails 0 time fails 0'. hops('zz','a',nodes)=-1, hops('a','b',null)=-1, inReach(null,...)=false, inReach({nodeId:'a'} /*no radius*/,...)=false. tariffCap(0)=100 and tariffCap(undefined)=100, which matches sql/038's meridian_base_floor 40 * meridian_tariff_mult 2.5 exactly. R.quote(5-hop).etaText = '10m' vs sql/038:826 'v_eta := v_hops * v_cfg.minutes_per_hop' with minutes_per_hop default 25 -> 125 minutes. R.quote({fromId:'a',toId:'a'}) returns {ok:true, hops:0, price:500} vs sql/038:744 'if p_from_node = p_to_node then return ... error, same_node'. sql/038:761 'v_mer_price := ceil(v_mer_base * v_units * v_hops)' vs routes.js:709 'price = refPrice + max(1, minPriceEdge)'. sql/038 mtime 03:00:36, index.js 03:04:44, routes.js 03:11:32 - the authority was readable.
